title: Chicago combo work: the Chocolate Music Bars hotel tours
summary: In Chicago he moved to combos and formed the Chocolate Music Bars, touring hotel and cocktail jobs in the Midwest.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: And in Chicago what type of music did you do?

Well, I got away from bands. They had a lot of three pieces, four pieces of combo in the yard. And I got with a fellow named Melvin Banks and we got with a fellow named John Creech, Papa John Creech, he played up at the Roses. And we organized a group, we called ourselves the Chocolate Music Balls. And we got jobs through bookings, some jobs came through the union, and we would go on, well, not tour, because we'd be working for a hotel chain, and we'd probably be, which would maybe be four weeks, six weeks, or eight weeks. We'd play most of the time, if it was four weeks or eight weeks, they'd hold us long, long, you see. And we did a lot of those, and I know we played Fort Wayne, we know we played Indianapolis, we went a way up in north of South Dakota, and a lot of other places, I can't mention, mention, mention, all in the northeastern state, from the Orleans, you see. At that time, most places had, they didn't have, besides, most places didn't, too, they have dance ball going on, but they had started with cocktail music, see. It's hotels, or they might be in a certain restaurant, a popular restaurant or something. They may walk me out, one of the places, they played quite a bit. Oh, yeah.
